title: Drop and Debt
premise: Coral Hartwell, a fixer for the Meridian Group — an embassy that exists on no map and no ledger — has been running on caffeine and guilt since a botched extraction left her partner dead. When the Group's most secret safe house appears on a real estate site with interior photos, Coral realizes someone inside sold them out, and the listing's metadata hides coordinates for an attack staged to look like a gas main failure. Racing a countdown she can barely read, Coral assembles a ragtag crew of exiles, liars, and one person she swore never to trust again, discovering along the way that the found family she built is both her greatest asset and the lever being used against her. In the end, Coral must choose between exposing the Group's complicity in the plot — burning every loyalty she has — or letting the truth die to save the people she loves; she finds a third path, at devastating cost, stopping the attack but going underground with her chosen family, hunted by the institution that made her.
about_author: Theo Okonkwo spent six years in logistics for humanitarian missions before turning to fiction, a career that taught him how institutions bury their mistakes. He writes from a different city every few months, claiming he works best where no one knows his face.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Insomniac Coral reviews routine asset disposal paperwork, then freezes: Safe House Kestrel — the site of 'the incident' — is listed on a public real estate site, complete with interior photos showing classified equipment. Her handler dismisses it as a glitch. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into certainty: nothing about this is accidental.

chapters.title: Metadata and Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Pulling the listing's hidden EXIF data, Coral finds geotags pointing not to the house but to a decommissioned water treatment plant downtown — and a timestamp eleven days out. She recognizes the staging pattern from the incident that killed her partner, Dev. Beat: guilt rekindled; she can't report up without admitting she kept copies of forbidden files.

chapters.title: The Handler's Smile
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Coral's handler, Voss, orders her to stand down and take mandatory leave — suspiciously generous leave. She obeys outwardly while copying the case file. A quiet scene with her neighbor Marisol, who feeds her when she forgets, shows the fragile found family anchoring her. Beat: loneliness versus the pull of connection.

chapters.title: Sixteen Days of Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Introduce Idris Okoye, Coral's former partner-in-the-field and the man she reported for negligence during Dev's death. Now a private security consultant, he receives an anonymous contract to 'consult' on venue security at the water plant — the same target. Beat: unease; he takes the job anyway because his debts demand it.

chapters.title: Old Wounds, New Addresses
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Coral tracks the real estate agent who listed Kestrel and finds her dead in an apparent overdose — three days before the listing went live. Someone is using dead people's identities. Beat: cold fury; Coral realizes the enemy knows the Group's tradecraft intimately, meaning it's one of their own.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Idris's employer, a shell company called Halcyon Risk, pays too well and asks too little. Digging into their contract, he finds clauses referencing 'atmospheric remediation' — a euphemism he last saw in a leaked memo about engineered gas failures. Beat: dawning horror as he connects his job to a mass-casualty plan.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Vault
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Coral/Idris. Both break into the same Halcyon records office on the same night and collide. Forced to flee together, they trade accusations about Dev's death mid-getaway. Beat: volatile chemistry — hatred and trust tangled, neither willing to walk away from what they've learned.

chapters.title: What Dev Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Decoding files Coral salvaged from Kestrel before it burned, they discover Dev had found the original Halcyon plan and was silenced — and that Coral's own report, the one that damned Idris, was doctored by Voss. Beat: shattering reversal; Coral's guilt was manufactured, and Idris's rage curdles into something more dangerous: purpose.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Table Council
chapters.summary: POV: ensemble via Coral. Coral convenes her off-book network in Marisol's kitchen: a disgraced forensic accountant, a teenage hacker named Junie who owes Coral her life, and a retired bomb tech called Pilar. They map the attack: a gas-main 'accident' timed to a city inspection tour. Beat: warmth and resolve — the found family formalizes into a team.

chapters.title: Voss Knows
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Summoned to a sterile meeting room, Coral faces Voss, who reveals he knows about her investigation and offers her a choice: help the Group contain Halcyon quietly and be restored, or continue and be disavowed. He hints the Group may have tolerated Halcyon once, long ago. Beat: temptation and suspicion braided together.

chapters.title: Junie's Mistake
chapters.summary: POV: Junie. Junie pings Halcyon's servers to confirm the attack date and trips a tripwire; a kill-team hits her safehouse within hours. Coral extracts her through storm drains, taking a knife wound. Beat: terror and tenderness — Coral realizes loving people makes them targets, and does it anyway.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Idris plays double agent inside Halcyon, feeding the team details: the attack uses industrial gas canisters routed through a legitimate utility contractor, scheduled during the inspection tour in four days. His handler grows suspicious of his questions. Beat: tightrope tension; one wrong word ends him.

chapters.title: The Doctored Report
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Following the forgery trail, Coral proves Voss personally altered her incident report — not to protect Halcyon, but because Voss helped design the original Kestrel operation Halcyon now mirrors. The Group isn't compromised; it's implicated. Beat: betrayal crystallized; there is no 'up' to report to.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Currency
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Halcyon moves the timeline up two days after detecting surveillance. Idris must warn the team without blowing his cover, so he engineers a fake emergency audit. Beat: sacrifice — he burns months of careful work in ninety seconds, knowing there's no way back inside.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. The team splits tasks under crushing time pressure: Pilar on the canisters, Junie on the utility's control systems, the accountant tracing money to identify the trigger-man. Coral plans to confront Voss with evidence simultaneously, forcing the Group to choose sides publicly. Beat: grim competence masking fear.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. The money trail leads to Deputy Inspector Renner — the official leading the inspection tour, who will 'survive' the accident as a hero and push through Halcyon-friendly contracts. Coral approaches him; he's not a believer, just a debtor, and cracks when shown proof his family is Halcyon's collateral if he talks. Beat: moral rot exposed; even villains are leverage.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Day one of the operation: the team intercepts the canister convoy using Renner's credentials, but Halcyon anticipated interference — a second, unlisted shipment is already inside the plant. Pilar is captured disabling the first cache. Beat: the plan collapses; despair sets in.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Halcyon offers Pilar's life for the evidence and for Coral herself. Against the team's pleas, Coral agrees to the exchange — but secretly loads the evidence to Junie's distributed dead-man's-switch, so surrendering costs her nothing permanent. Beat: love against duty made literal; she chooses her people over her safety and her cause over her leverage.

chapters.title: The Water Plant
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. The exchange goes wrong when Voss arrives with a Group strike team, intending to erase everyone — Coral, Halcyon, the evidence. Three-way standoff in the pump halls. Idris turns his insider access against Halcyon's trigger-man; Pilar frees herself in the chaos. Beat: controlled chaos, alliances shifting by the second.

chapters.title: Vent
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Climax part one: with minutes before the second cache vents, Coral and Idris descend into the plant's flooded lower levels — the same layout as Kestrel, deliberately chosen to break her. Confronting the Halcyon architect, Coral learns Voss commissioned the whole plot to force the Group to purge its own rot with him at the top. Beat: the past made physical; she refuses to repeat it.

chapters.title: Accidents of Their Own
chapters.summary: POV: Idris. Climax part two: they vent the canisters harmlessly into the water system, then let Halcyon's own failsafe destroy the cache — an 'accident' that kills the architect and buries the operation. Voss escapes the blast but finds his authority gone: Renner, flipped, has already delivered Coral's evidence to three governments. Beat: catharsis through the enemy's own methods turned back on them.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: POV: Coral. Resolution: the Group disavows Coral rather than face exposure; she expected it. Voss vanishes, a loose thread she chooses to stop chasing. The team gathers at Marisol's table — Pilar teaching Junie lock-picking, Idris finally sleeping through the night beside Coral. A new safe house listing appears online: theirs, photos and all, a warning and an invitation. Beat: hard-won peace, vigilance, and belonging; the family is the safe house now.
